title: Kernel stratification and attention-fusion hardening after capacity-induced P99 regression
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a high-concurrency capacity surge on 2025-02-09 we observed a sharp P99 latency regression for chat generation routes backed by fused attention kernels. The scheduler's kernel-stratification heuristic began selecting a speculative, unfused attention kernel for a subset of requests under bursty arrivals. That kernel has higher per-token CPU/GPU scheduling overhead at short sequence lengths, which amplified tail latency and caused request queueing in some worker pools. This ticket tracks the follow-ups, mitigations, and longer-term hardening to prevent recurrence.
impact_details: Impacted routes: /v1/generate-chat (small-batch, short-context), affected customers: several PLG customers on hosted tier experienced transient 2-4x P99 increases between 02:15–03:20 UTC. Alerts triggered: p99-latency-rise, scheduler-path-oscillation. No data loss; requests were delayed but eventually served. Estimated lost SLA: ~0.2% of requests exceeded 1s SLO during window.
root_cause: The scheduler's stratification logic included a transient probe that promotes alternate kernels when observed throughput drops. During the capacity event, a combination of probe amplification + autoscaler assign churn allowed a small fraction of requests to be routed to an unfused attention kernel which performs worse at short seq lengths due to reduced fused matmul/softmax path utilization. Hysteresis and cost-model weighting for sequence-length distribution were insufficient under burst arrivals leading to an incorrect ranking.
mitigation_summary: Immediate: rolled back the nightly kernel-rank heuristic change at 02:40 UTC (runtime rollback: revert PR #1187). Disabled speculative probe window for fused-attn family and rebalanced kernel weights. Medium-term: deployed an emergency canary that enforces sequence-length aware ranking in scheduler (PR #1193). Long-term: add deterministic warm-up, new offline benchmarking, and improved canary/rollback automation.
actions: A1: Patch scheduler to include sequence-length conditional weight and 10s hysteresis (owner: Liam O'Connor) — target: 2025-02-24 — trackers: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1193
A2: Reintroduce a bounded speculative probe with rate limit and exponential backoff; circuit-breaker when p99 increases are observed (owner: Priya Narang) — target: 2025-03-01 — issue: ENG-881238

A3: Add small-batch fused-attn microbenchmarks to CI with synthetic short-seq traffic to catch regressions (owner: Diego Alvarez) — target: 2025-02-28 — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/224

A4: Expand canary dashboard for kernel-ranking to include sequence-length heatmap and per-kernel tail percentiles (owner: Sara Kim) — target: 2025-02-26 — Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/kernel-ranking

A5: Update rollout playbook to require 24h gated canary for kernel-ranking changes; automated rollback trigger at +20% p99 (owner: Ops) — target: 2025-03-05 — Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Rollout+Playbook
A6: Audit autoscaler+assignment interactions with scheduler probes and introduce slot stabilization (owner: Carlos Mendes) — target: 2025-03-10 — dependency: ENG-421007
A7: Implement traffic-rewrite test harness to reproduce bursty arrival patterns in staging (owner: Maya Chen) — target: 2025-02-21 — repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/staging-load-generators
A8: Postmortem doc and customer-facing summary (owner: Kate Sullivan) — target: 2025-02-18 — draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B-example
updates: 2025-02-09 02:22 UTC — Oncall alerted on p99 increase. Initial triage pointed to sudden kernel-selection divergence in scheduler metrics.
2025-02-09 02:35 UTC — Emergency rollback of kernel-rank heuristic applied (runtime revert PR #1187). p99 began degrading back to baseline within 5 minutes after disabling probes.
2025-02-09 03:05 UTC — Hotfix deployed: disabled speculative probe windows for fused-attn family, added temporary cap on kernel-switch rate (PR #1189).

2025-02-10 09:12 UTC — Investigations show sequence-length distribution skew during the burst; replayed sample traces in a replay cluster and reproduced 2.3x p99 increase when unfused kernels were selected.
2025-02-12 15:43 UTC — Design review: agreed to add sequence-aware ranking and hysteresis; accepted by runtime and scheduler owners. Notes: prioritize quick/low-risk changes then iterate.
2025-02-18 18:27 UTC — Canary config pushed to a 1% slice in us-west; initial observations look good. No customer-facing regressions observed in canary.
2025-02-21 11:00 UTC — This ticket opened to track all follow-ups and consolidate action items after the incident retro.
postmortem_notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive speculative probing improves throughput for cold kernels but increases risk under assignment churn; we prefer conservative probes with reliable fallback for hosted customers.
We discovered gaps in our synthetic workloads: synthetic benchmarks favored steady-state throughput but did not mimic bursty short-seq chat traffic. We'll expand the workload matrix.
Ownership: scheduler heuristics live with the serving runtime team; cross-team coordination with autoscaler and infra is required to resolve assignment/probe interactions.
review_feedback: PM review (A. Gupta): please include customer-impact timeline for support to reference in communications.
Design review (Sara Kim): suggest adding per-model quantile expectations to the canary dashboard so we can detect skewed distributions earlier.
Security review (T. Huang): no secrets exposed; confirm KMS interactions unaffected.
Eng review (Diego Alvarez): include microbenchmark PR numbers and make sure CI gating is strict before merging ranking changes.
notes: Do not re-enable the previous probing parameters without a staged rollout and explicit canary validation for short-sequence workloads.
When closing, include a follow-up ticket that measures customer token-cost impact of the new ranking to validate cost regressions do not occur.
